title: Timestamp Before Signal
youtube_title: Timestamp Before Signal: Why Data Time Matters
instagram_caption: A chart is only as useful as the time behind it. Check the bar timestamp, session, source, and freshness before treating a signal as evidence. Paper-trading education only; not live-money performance; not investment advice; no guaranteed returns. #AMORDER #MarketData #DataQuality

scenes.title: A timestamp is evidence
scenes.narration: Before a signal means anything, confirm when the data was recorded. A bar without a trustworthy timestamp is not reliable evidence.

scenes.title: Know the source
scenes.narration: Check the market source, the trading session, and whether the quote belongs to the market you intend to study.

scenes.title: Stale data changes the picture
scenes.narration: Stale quotes, missing bars, or gaps in history can make a clean chart look more certain than it really is.

scenes.title: A signal is a hypothesis
scenes.narration: A setup score is a hypothesis to test. It is not a fill, not a return, and not a reason to skip the evidence check.

scenes.title: Measure before acting
scenes.narration: Use completed data, fresh quotes, and known market conditions before you decide whether an entry is even eligible.

scenes.title: Pause when time is unclear
scenes.narration: If the timestamp or source cannot be verified, standing down is the disciplined result. The process does not need a trade every day.
